title: Eviction watchdog: heartbeat rescue and rate-ramp limiter
author: Priya Nair
description:
Context: Recent incidents showed noisy mass-evictions when transient node stalls caused the scheduler to treat nodes as unhealthy. This led to large tenant ejects and subsequent rejoin storms that amplified load on remaining nodes. Motivation: introduce a lightweight eviction "watchdog" that interposes a heartbeat-rescue path before performing tenant-level evictions, and a rate-ramp limiter that soft-throttles reinstatement/rejoin to avoid surge. This PR implements the runtime guard, operator-configurable thresholds, and an emergency feature-flag for immediate rollback. Changes are intentionally conservative: default behavior only adds a two-stage check and a slow ramp for tenant reconnects; full hard-fail evictions are unchanged behind the same feature flag.

What this PR does: 1) Eviction Watchdog: when node health probes detect a stall, we attempt a heartbeat-rescue: a lightweight liveness probe that performs a KV-cache-preserving drain step (try_graceful_drain) and defers tenant eviction for a short, configurable window (default 15s). If the node remains unresponsive, eviction proceeds as before. 2) Rate-ramp limiter: after evictions/reinstatements, tenant rejoin is paced using a token-bucket-like ramp that increases allowed rejoin rate over a configurable warmup period (default 120s). 3) Tenant hedging: critical-tenants list (operator-managed) gets prioritized soft-paths to minimize user-visible latency during graceful degradation. 4) Observability: new metrics (watchdog_attempts_total, watchdog_succeeds_total, rejoin_ramp_current_rate, rejoin_ramp_allowed_tokens) and traces for the rescue path. 5) Feature flag and rollout: runtime flag `eviction_watchdog.v1` (off by default) and k8s config map knobs for thresholds.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of watchdog rescue flow - [x] Rate-ramp and config knobs - [x] Unit tests for rescue and pacing logic - [x] Integration test exercising graceful drain without eviction - [x] E2E canary run plan documented - [x] Metrics and tracing added - [x] Docs and operator playbook note added in repo `docs/operational` (short note)

Testing & rollout notes: local unit/integration, then canary in us-west-2 with 5% traffic for 48h; if no regressions, ramp to 25% then 100% over 72h. Feature flag allows rollback to previous eviction behavior instantly. If telemetry shows >1.5x rejoin failures or sustained token exhaust, we will disable the feature flag and revert change.

review_conversation: Ethan Park (reviewer): Nice approach — can we make the RescueWindow configurable per-region? Some regions have longer cold-starts due to networking.
Author (Priya): Yes, added region_override in the config map and documented recommended defaults for low-latency regions.
Maya Alvarez (reviewer): Unit tests look good. Integration test flaked once in CI (timing). Recommend increasing test timeouts and adding deterministic fake clock.
Author (Priya): Added fake clock to ramp_limiter_test and bumped timeouts in the integration harness. CI run is green now.
Rui Zhao (approver): Approving after minor nits. Please add a short note in the operator playbook about disabling the flag under token exhaustion.
Author (Priya): Added operator playbook note and an emergency rollback snippet (kubectl patch to turn flag off).
Infra (comment): Observability team requested a tag on the histogram for tenant-criticality to help correlate incidents.
Author (Priya): Added tenant_criticality label to rejoin_ramp_current_rate metric; tests updated accordingly.
release_notes: Introduce Eviction Watchdog: a rescue heartbeat step before eviction plus a rejoin rate-ramp limiter. Defaults are conservative and gated behind feature flag eviction_watchdog.v1. Operators should follow the docs/operational/eviction_watchdog.md playbook when enabling.
